correctness.rationale: With x=cos(theta), the height difference factors as (1−x)[−1+2a(1+x)+b(2x+1)²]. The coefficient vector is nonnegative on the entire cycle, so the Euclidean support-function maximum is exactly F_E(x)=E G(x)−(1−x). Independently, for x=−u, 0≤u≤1, the components whose norm is G(−u) are 2(1−u²) and (1+u)(1−2u)²=1−3u+4u³. Up to u=√3/2 the latter is at most 1 and the former at most 2; above that point they are bounded by 2 and 1/2 respectively in the opposite order. Thus G(−u)≤√5 and F_E(−u)≤F_E(0). Polynomial differentiation gives R G'=3+4x−8x²−48x³−48x⁴ and −R³ G''/4 with ascending coefficients 1,33,264,816,1392,1584,1152,384. On [0,1] this proves strict concavity for E>0, and F_E'(0)>0 while F_E'(1)=1−E√97. The cases E=0 and E=1/√97 yield zero excess, with every allocation optimal in excess value, not a unique allocation. Above threshold there is a unique interior x_E; equality in the Euclidean norm bound forces the stated positive allocation and exactly two phases modulo the cycle. Positive excess requires 4a+9b>1, hence positive central curvature. The relation G'(x_E)=−1/E and strict concavity give strict decrease in x_E and the unique quartic limit (independent numerical check: 0.371708101121). As E approaches onset the amplitude direction tends to (4,9)/√97. The frozen symbolic/grid script was inspected but not executed; the result does not rely on its grids.

value.rationale: Rather than just identifying a local curvature threshold, this solves the full-cycle allocation problem and rules out a competing, remote high-water maximum. It gives a unique allocation above onset and a monotone crest-spacing prediction through the whole mathematical energy range. That is useful as a sharp benchmark within the phase-locked harmonic model, not a claim about real tidal forcing or attainable ocean energies.
